facts: USDJPY remains near 158.1 after the Tokyo open and after stronger real-wage data.
The wage data were yen-supportive in principle, but the immediate FX move was small.
Early JGB futures were firmer rather than selling off, so Japan yields are not providing a fresh upside shock to JPY.
The pair has not yet broken yesterday's 158.25 high or the nearby 158.5 resistance area.
interpretations: The 07:54 NEUTRAL_TO_SLIGHT_USDJPY_UP view remains broadly intact, but conviction should be reduced because stronger Japanese real wages add a legitimate yen-supportive input.
The failure of USDJPY to fall materially on favorable Japanese wage data again points to underlying yen weakness / limited near-term BOJ repricing.
A clean break above 158.25-158.5 would strengthen the upside case; failure there and a move below 157.9 would shift the state back toward neutral/down.
The next major global catalyst remains the FOMC minutes tonight; morning BOJ/MOF statistical releases appear secondary so far.
change_since_prior: MODEST_CHANGE: stronger Japanese real-wage data caused only a small USDJPY dip from around 158.17 to roughly 158.08, while JGB futures were firm. The pair remains resilient near 158.1.
base_case: NEUTRAL_TO_SLIGHT_USDJPY_UP, but with lower conviction than at 07:54 because the wage data strengthen the yen-supportive macro case.
alternative_case: USDJPY_DOWN if 158.25-158.5 resistance holds and Tokyo trading transmits the stronger wage/BOJ-normalization story into firmer JPY.
